pr_title: storage: update min version with store cluster version
pr_body:
Whenever the store cluster version key is updated, update the minimum
storage version too.

Fix #69116.

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/69203)

> To clarify, we're not proposing only writing the file at open time exclusively. We're proposing within the bootstrap/join code path, only writing the file before open.

Makes sense -- I didn't realize that earlier

> We need to either
a) explicitly tell the storage engine that it's ok to upgrade its version now
b) commit to the cluster's version before we open the storage engine
> Since we don't appear to have any real need for opening the storage engine before committing to the cluster version, we're proposing going with option b.

- Do we get the cluster version by talking to other nodes?
- And if the cluster is being upgraded and a new node is started during that upgrade, there could be a race where it sees an old version. But that would be harmless because it would eventually see the upgraded version and do this write to the min version, yes?
- What happens with multiple stores in a node? Can their cluster versions diverge, and do we only use cluster version for behavior adjustment on a per store basis?

issue_context.title: storage: monolithic encryption-at-rest registry not disabled for new clusters
issue_context.body:
When creating a new CockroachDB node or cluster with encryption-at-rest turned after #67320, both the old monolithic Base version registry and the new incremental Records version registry are created, and the version of the registry remains as Base. This is due to the fact that the migration that deprecates the old registry and writes the `STORAGE_MIN_VERSION` file is not run for new clusters.

This should be fixed before 21.2 is released and any potential solutions may want to take into consideration that any new clusters that were created after #67320 may contain both the old and new registry files despite not needing the old one.

cc @jbowens

review_comments:
nit: we don't write to the engine today (at least according to my reading of the code). What we would need to change is that the engine is either created only as part of bootstrap/join (this is not done today due to plumbing reasons, some of which historical) or "unwriteable" before bootstrap/join (slightly less clean solution, but gives the right guarantees). We can effectively "enforce" (at least heuristically) the latter invariant today, which I would ask you to consider.

In https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/e915cb0aef63e498bdc5ff86807cfb8f6f0fe21a/pkg/server/init.go#L495 and https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/e915cb0aef63e498bdc5ff86807cfb8f6f0fe21a/pkg/server/init.go#L517 we should check that all engines (they are all in `unitializedEngines`) are completely empty, i.e. have never been issued a write op to (or whichever other condition you like most - the goal is to make sure that the engine is pretty much as good as one that was *just* created). If they are not, an error is returned. If this fails in any test, we'll know that there is a problem.

I might be misreading, but I think this call will at least write to the store version key in advance of boostrapping/joining: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/e915cb0aef63e498bdc5ff86807cfb8f6f0fe21a/pkg/server/server.go#L1233-L1237 

If we eventually begin to use the separate storage version file exclusively, it seems like we could assert the engine is completely empty. I'll do some more sleuthing; maybe we should just assert that the engine contains no keys other than the store cluster key.

That's a good point. I think we could avoid this write somehow in the case you care about (all engines empty) and delay it to where we first initialize the engines anyway. But checking that the engine is empty mod this one key is a good cheap way to be done with it now, too.
Updated to check the engine is empty modulo the store cluster key for now.
It's interesting, I think this would basically obviate StoreClusterVersionKey above, mod some details (we have code that backfills the version between all stores, etc)
